question.text: Per Regulation 23 of SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012, Category I and Category II AIFs must undertake valuation of their investments:

answer.text: At least once every 3 months by the AIF's internal valuer
Daily NAV computation as per mutual fund regulations
At least once every 6 months by an independent valuer; extendable to once a year with 75% investor approval by value
Only at entry and exit of each investee company

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 23(2) explicitly requires Cat I and Cat II AIFs to value investments AT LEAST once every SIX months by an independent valuer. The frequency can be EXTENDED to one year with approval of at least 75% of investors by value. The PDF Section 11.11 reproduces this verbatim. The Trap: 3 months with internal valuer is wrong on both counts (must be independent, 6-month minimum); daily NAV is Cat III / mutual fund territory; entry-exit only misses periodic mark-to-market. Remember: Cat I/II = 6 months minimum, Cat III = daily NAV. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same frequency. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests daily NAV obligation for Cat III. This 6-monthly vs daily distinction is the most-tested regulatory boundary between Cat I/II and Cat III. Manager's Pro-Tip: Plan your valuer engagement calendar at fund close. Two cycles per year (typically Sep 30 and Mar 31) align with financial year reporting. Budget for the valuer's fee in your fund expenses from Year 1 — it is a scheme expense, not a Manager expense.
